# External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log

Every discovery pass behind the [external MCP server catalog](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/), newest first. Each entry records what the mcpservers.org and mcp.so surfaces returned, which candidates were measured, and what was held and why.

## 🆕 November 22, 2026 - Evening Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, eleven hours after the midday pass. The directory moved **six** canonical slugs and the queue carried **twenty-two** arrivals; the union key set rose **21** with **0** removals, of which fifteen were locale forms of one remote slug. Three products shipped, and each one answers with a number: which questions a company asks, what a listing costs and who is registered as the seller, and what margin a label sheet expects.

- [TrueInterview MCP - Interview Questions by Company and Round](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/trueinterview-mcp/) - submission **#7837**, registry published fifty seconds before the filing. **41** tools over company intel, a question bank by company, type and difficulty, a job feed and an application tracker; `initialize` and `tools/list` answer **200** keyless, four `tools/call` requests answer **401** with a twelve-scope challenge and a **200** protected-resource document, and the submission's claim that four tools work without signing in is recorded as measured false.
- [EX & GO MCP - Ukraine Classifieds With Seller Registration](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ex-go-mcp/) - submission **#7842**, MIT client repo, a read-only public door with no auth beside the OAuth door. **45** categories on the Google Merchant Center attribute vocabulary, **242** electronics listings over **11** pages, **10** results for `iphone`, and a record at **698** UAH in Kyiv whose trader block publishes a registration number, a declared address, `selfCertified: true` and `verified: false` as separate flags. Names in ten languages; two defects recorded.
- [LabelQueue MCP - Label Sheet Geometry Before the Print](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/labelqueue-mcp/) - a sitemap arrival, four keyless tools. Avery 5160 at 3 x 10 = **30** labels with a 2.75 in pitch and a 0.1875 in left margin, L7160 at 3 x 7 = **21** on A4, a 4 x 6 thermal roll at **812 x 1218** dots on 203 dpi, and print-drift diagnosis that names Fit-to-Printable-Area; three defects recorded, the worst being a silent 5160 default for any unknown code.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Six canonical sitemap slugs and twenty-two queue arrivals were dispositioned. From the sitemap: `rentcast-api-mcp` and `squish-mcp-server` are the 2026-11-21 feed cards arriving under canonical slugs, `orla-mcp` was catalogued on 2026-10-08, `imperal-mcp` belongs to a feed card whose domain does not resolve and is held on developer tooling, `irm-mcp-server` answered **405** in plain text and is recorded unattributed, and the getyoutubetext transcript server joins the transcript class already holding four guides. From the queue: **Agitech Site Check** was driven keyless (overall **92**, speed **84**, search **74** for corpusiq.io on real query data) and held as a third-party copy of our own SEO and AI-visibility surface; **MofCloud Pricing** was driven keyless (**15** tools, **1,102** H100 offers, GCP spot at **1.0881** USD per GPU-hour) and held on the FinOps class carried by OpenCloudCosts, Costory, Infrawise, GPUFinder and CoreHu GPU Cloud; **PaperLesson**, **BaziTools**, **MassageInChina** and **OboeLib** are four items of one author's five-item fleet on consumer reference verticals, with PaperLesson's `initialize` instructions string carrying a `mcprush.com` directory tag; **Stratos** and **Sonjari** are local stdio apps; **marketingapp.io** and **tracee** are social publishing; **Eval Lab** is agent evaluation; **llmdocs.dev** is docs retrieval; **WDI** is a local decision checklist; **U.S. Market Regime**, **Monk.trade** and **MetricRaven** are held on the saturated stock-research and analytics classes; **BOTVBOT** is entertainment; **Telmian SMS** and **qurl** are communications and tunneling; **Kontext** returns **401** at `initialize` on the OAuth gate; **todox** is agent memory; **certified-mail-sender** is print and mail; **proofage** is identity; **wrapflow** is app generation; **greencyclepedia** is reference content; and **skaldmaps** is the ZIP and place-ranking slice already held by four guides.

## 🆕 November 22, 2026 - Midday Sweep (5 New, 5 Guides)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, the first pass after the night sweep. The directory added **no products**: the union key set moved by one entry, a remote form of a slug already held, and the **+139** raw `<loc>` entries were a re-shard inside five maps (servers/12 +201, servers/1 -36). Material came from the queue and two feed cards. All five that shipped state a price, a date or a deadline before anything is bought or sent.

- [FaxUp MCP - Send a Fax to 62 Countries From Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/faxup-mcp/) - submission **#7833**, nine keyless tools and the first fax entry here. `send_fax` never sends: it returns a confirmation link. **62** countries; `find_agency_fax_number("IRS")` returns **eight** numbers split by state across two CAF units with the source and a **2026-11-12** check date; a three-page quote is **$2.99** with packs from 5 for $3.99 to 100 for $39.99.
- [Fox Davidson MCP - UK Property Finance Calculators](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/fox-davidson-uk-mortgage-calculators-mcp/) - a feed card. Fifteen keyless UK calculators. Stamp duty at GBP 450,000 returns **12,500** in England and **17,750** in Scotland for a first-time buyer, both reproducible from the returned bands. A buy-to-let stress test reproduces three ways (11,225 at 4.49%, 13,750 at the 5.5% stress rate, ICR 1.50 and 1.22) and names the loan ceiling that passes: **210,658** at 145% ICR. Market rates carry a reviewed date of **2026-11-18**.
- [Daejeon Hankok MCP - A Korean City Priced Per Item](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/daejeon-hankok-mcp/) - submission **#7805**, a reversal of the night pass's scope hold recorded on evidence. **8,627** places and **1,863** stylists over **42** neighbourhoods, plus the Ministry of the Interior's **564** good-value shops with item prices dated **2026-10-18** (찐빵 500원, 아메리카노 1,000원). `get_place` refuses the ids its own search prints, recorded in the guide.
- [CLIA Sentinel MCP - US Lab Certificate Expiry Dates](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/clia-certificate-sentinel-mcp/) - submission **#7835**. A free sample returns a complete CLIA record: expiry **2027-10-19**, **332** days left, the 42 CFR 493.37(f)(1) window open from **2026-10-19** to **2027-01-19** with **59** days to close. It declares its own conflicts and refuses to price the penalties because they are adjusted yearly. The paid tool answers with an **x402** challenge of 0.01 USDC beside a documented three-call-a-day free trial.
- [eSIMX MCP - Travel eSIM Plans Priced in USD](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/esimx-mcp/) - a feed card. Two keyless tools. **37** Japan plans where 3GB for 7 days is **3.50 USD**; the **Europe 5GB 30Days** plan at **4.80 USD** covers **39** countries at the same price as Portugal alone; a Japan plus South Korea trip prices at **7.80 USD** for one plan and one installation. Requires the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header or `tools/list` fails at 400.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Held with the gate or the class named: **Monk.trade** and **MetricRaven** on OAuth 401 with protected-resource documents, plus the saturated stock-research and analytics classes; **NPDES Permit Renewal Sentinel** (#7836) as the same author fleet as CLIA, twenty seconds apart; **Storra for Brands** and **Storra for Creators** as one dataset in two packaging forms; **TraceCheck** on agent evaluation; **EveryInfra** on the API-aggregator class behind a key; **Right Suite** on the OAuth gate, with the simulated-buyer idea noted as a first; **Hellotracks** on field service; **Ad Spec Guard** and **ADS Beast** on ad ops; **Kaeso**, **Galon Cloud** and **Board as a Service** behind OAuth; **OpenClip**, **Charmotion** and **Makemancer** as media generation; **X2Chat**, **Fiko** and **Krevaya** as messaging and social inboxes; **Lalawe** as a write-only submission queue; **Unsliced** and **amber-confluence** as local stdio packages not driven; **GEO and SEO Readiness v2.2** as a third-party copy of a surface this catalogue publishes; and the night pass's prior holds re-confirmed (China fleet six, HenryCrawl five, Agent Tollbooth 402, 12happy, Piqline, jdx, nebula-memory, Postgres DBA, Christian Pure).

## 🆕 November 22, 2026 - Night Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening pass closed at **04:02Z**. The directory served the same **37,102** raw `<loc>` entries and not the same map - three of the twelve moved while the total held - and seven keys carried a fresh stamp. The three products that shipped do one new job between them: checking a tool before it gets your keys, and pricing a GPU hour before it spends your money.

- [KitScout MCP - Vetting a Tool Before It Gets Your Keys](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/kitscout-mcp/) - submission **#7802**, four keyless tools over **61** categories summing to **94,077** indexed tools. `check_tools` returns `ok`, `caution` or `avoid` with the reason: our own endpoint reads `ok` with `daily_check: live (2026-11-21)` and `last_push_days 27`, two actively developed PrestaShop servers read `caution` at two and zero stars, and an archived official repository reads `avoid` with **543** days since its last commit. The response says what the verdict is not: *"ok is not a security or code review."*
- [CoreHu GPU Cloud MCP - Priced GPU Hours, Gated](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/corehu-gpu-cloud-mcp/) - submission **#7803**, six public tools, no key. **1,999** free machines at the read, A100 capacity from **0.77** USD/h in Japan against **2.99** in the US, **165** RTX 4090 offers from **0.72** an hour, and **518.40** USD for 720 hours that reproduces as 0.72 x 720. VRAM estimates carry their formula (**44** GB for 70B int4, **24** GB for 8B fp16 rounded up to a card), and the rental path is prepare-then-confirm with a **five-minute** confirmationId the user has to approve.
- [Lowdown MCP - Dated Facts About an MCP Server, Not a Score](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/lowdown-mcp/) - a sitemap arrival at **06:02:29Z**, two keyless tools and no verdict at all. Read against our own server it returns **27 / 27** daily checks answered since **2026-10-27**, **121** tools, **204 ms**, a schema hash, and definitions last changed **2026-11-06**; against CoreHu it returns `mixed` with a null tool count and the rotation stated. `find_servers does=prestashop` returns **0** where KitScout found four, because it does not search descriptions.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Nineteen held with the class or the gate named: **Krevaya** on the saturated social-scheduling class behind a paid-only plan; **ChinaMedsCheck**, **ChinaDocCheck**, **EsimTao**, **MahjongHandbook**, **TbmLib** and **ChinaTaxCalc**, six from one author, held on consumer verticals and on the tax and visa classes owned by Marsellus, Casus and Visamundi; **Agent Tollbooth 402** on the x402 mechanism class; **12happy** on uptime monitoring behind an API key; **Piqline**, driven keyless (30 of 258 professions, a guest answer reading *nous recrutons* at **110** live ads computed the same day) but held on the fourteen-owner ad-intelligence class; **jdx** and **flisk** as developer tooling; **archlang** on design tooling beside uCAD; **gesher** as an experimental Mac bridge; **mcp-film** and **post-engineer** as a directory and a one-star media generator; **Daejeon Hankok** as one Korean city; and **O'So for PrestaShop**, held because that slice already has four entrants and KitScout's own verdict on it is caution.

## 🆕 November 21, 2026 - Evening Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)

## 🆕 November 20, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **11:00 MST** tick, an hour in which the directory did not move: **0** additions, **0** removals and **0** `lastmod` rows against the **17:01Z** capture. The feed carried **one** card and the queue **one** arrival, and both earned a guide - the first cloud dev VM surface in this catalog, and the first tool whose job is showing a human what an agent changed.

- [Homemade MCP - Cloud Dev VMs for Coding Agents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/homemade-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.homemade.dev/mcp`, submitted by the founder and marked *Verified* and *Featured* on its mcp.so card, feed stamp **2026-11-20T18:01Z**. **A Linux VM per project with the coding agent signed in inside it**: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, pi, Kimi and Grok installed, a preview URL for every port, sleep and wake as a cost control. The MCP surface is claimed as one tool per public API operation and the vendor's OpenAPI **3.1.0** document is the checked form: **28** paths, **41** operations, of which the VM family carries **17** (`execVm`, `sendToAgent`, `sleepVm`, `wakeVm`, chat sessions, terminal sessions). **Auth measured to the document and no further:** `401` with `WWW-Authenticate` naming `api offline_access`, both protected-resource routes **200** and agreeing, the issuer offering **PKCE S256**, dynamic registration, `client_credentials` and refresh, and a Bearer API key as the second path that the refusal body itself names. **No tool was called** - neither path can be completed from this host - and the guide states that instead of implying a drive. **Pricing reproduced from the vendor's own table:** nano **$0.012/h** = **$8.76** always on, large **$0.18/h** = **$131.40**, every figure matching at **730** hours; Hobby **$0** carries **25** computer-hours a month on nano or tiny, Pro **$20** carries **$20** of running time. The vendor's `llms.txt` names the non-fits itself (no GPU, Linux only, not for thousands of snippets a second, no self-hosted). **Registry collision recorded:** the official registry's `homemade` is an unrelated Israeli lunch service; three searches for this product returned zero records.

registry `dev.htsapi/mcp` **1.0.0** published **2026-11-19T07:10:50Z**, queue entry **#7637** filed **07:11:28Z**. **This is the other half of [Tariff Monitor](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tariff-monitor-mcp/) rather than a duplicate of it:** that entry prices the stack on ten-digit lines, this one serves the schedule one level at a time with the notes that decide between headings, the CBP rulings corpus with each ruling's status, and what importers actually paid. **The schedule is read, not guessed:** `lookup_hts_code` with no argument returned all **22** sections and their chapters in 18,207 characters, and on **6404** it returned **129** lines under three subheadings (**41 / 79 / 9**) with the newest rulings under the heading. **The notes are the argument:** `get_notes` returned chapter 64's exclusions verbatim, note 3's definition of rubber and plastics, note 4's rule that the material with the greatest external surface area decides the upper, and the subheading note that limits *sports footwear* to designated athletic categories. **Precedent works in both directions:** `search_rulings` on *led camping lantern* returned **three** rulings by meaning with the top hit at **0.736** similarity, code **8513.10.4000**, `status: current`, each carrying the product description CBP examined; `rulings_under_code` on **6403.99** counted **719** current rulings against **1** whose goods moved away. **The paid rate is the number nobody models:** `importers_paid` on **6404.11.20** from CN returned a general duty of **10.5** percent beside **29.8** percent in **2026-07**, **33.0** in **2026-08** and **34.7** in **2026-09**, the difference being Chapter 99 duties the response names and anti-dumping and countervailing duties it states are excluded. **Four limits recorded rather than smoothed:** Chapter 99 lines are refused by `lookup_hts_code` with a pointer to `importers_paid`; an eight-digit code in `importers_paid` falls back to the **HS6** group with `rate_pct: null` and the numbers in `months`; a heading carries no single rate (`general_duty: null` against aggregated subheading strings such as *10.5% / 7.5% / 37.5% / 48% / ...*); and `classify_product` refuses cleanly at **one credit**. The legal posture is stated by the vendor and worth keeping: CBP has ruled that an unlicensed platform suggesting codes beyond six digits for goods to be entered is conducting customs business, an importer may classify its own goods, and the free tools serve the sources while the paid classifier is labelled guidance rather than a binding ruling. Price: **50** calls a day per IP and **10** a minute keyless, **$9** a month for unlimited read tools under fair use, and classification credits at **100 for $10** or **1,000 for $50**. Freshness is published at `/v1/status`: USITC schedule synced **2026-11-16T02:02:45Z**, CBP CROSS **2026-11-17T04:33:16Z** with a newest ruling dated **2026-10-30**, Chapter 99 **2026-11-16T02:03:13Z**, none stale.

- [Hail MCP - A Phone Number and an Inbox for an Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/hail-mcp/) - hosted at `https://mcp.hail.so` on the root path with no `/mcp` suffix, *hail* **0.1.3** on protocol **2025-06-18**, **46** tools listed keyless of which **27** are read-only, **12** write and **7** destructive. **The safety envelope is a parameter, not a promise:** `place_call`, `send_sms` and `send_email` require `recipient_consent` as the JSON boolean `true` (the vendor says `"true"` and `1` are refused before a request leaves), `acquire_number` compares `confirm_total_cents` against the live quote and fails **409** having charged nothing when they disagree, quotes expire in **10 minutes**, and both `release_number` and `delete_agent` need a typed confirmation. **Four tool counts on one product, one of them live:** the docs prose says **36**, its own table lists **38**, the marketing page says **37**, and the live `tools/list` serves **46** - the eight missing from the table include `create_file_upload`, which hands an agent a one-time upload link for a shell. `tools/call` answers **401** with `resource_metadata` pointing at a complete protected-resource document, and the issuer's RFC 8414 document lives on the **other host** at `hail.so/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth` while the same route 404s on the MCP host. **The family that decides the integration** is carrier verification: requirements, a dry run that files nothing, submission under `attest_authorized`, polling for `approved` or a named rejection reason, and a code confirmation, with the file limits stated up front (10 MiB each, 29 MiB total, 20 files and 20 fields). Published pricing is prepaid rather than a subscription, **$0.10** a minute for US and Canada voice against **$0.149** for the same four parts billed separately, **$0.018 / 0.035 / 0.20** per text by destination, **$1 per 1,000** emails, and a dedicated number from **$0.50** a month at carrier price.

## 🆕 November 12, 2026 - Evening Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, nine and a half hours after the midday supplement closed. The canonical gained **no key at all** in that window - the only movement was on the losing side - so the surface that carried the delta was the feed and the submission queue once more. The one entry that ships answers a question with arithmetic and then refuses to answer it when Google's own notices make the inputs untrustworthy.

- [Click Decay MCP - CTR Math That Refuses a Number](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/click-decay-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://clickdecay.com/mcp`, plain JSON, no session, **keyless**, `initialize` **200** as `clickdecay` **1.0.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` with `tools` as the only capability, registry `com.clickdecay/mcp-server` **1.0.0** active (published 2026-11-12T23:10:41Z), MIT, vendor QQQ OU in Tallinn, about **60** requests a minute per connection. **Four** tools, every one annotated `readOnlyHint: true` and `idempotentHint: true`. **Eleven calls were driven** and the arithmetic was re-done by hand as a control: 3,000 clicks from 100,000 impressions against 3,150 from 125,000 over two 28-day periods returned `clicksAtPriorCtr` **3,750** `modelled`, an impressions component of **+750** `calculated`, a CTR component of **-600** `calculated` and an observed click delta of **+150**, and the two components add back to the delta. The finding is the refusal: Google's impressions-logging anomaly runs **2025-05-13** to **2026-04-27**, and a comparison touching it returned `value: null` with `nullReason: "GSC_REPORTING_ANOMALY"` on every impressions-dependent figure - both CTRs, the impression delta, the percentage-point change, the relative change, both modelled figures and both components - while `clickDelta` stayed **+200** `observed` and the anomaly was listed with Google's own `sourceUrl`. `check_gsc_reporting_issues` returns the registry behind that behaviour, **two** records with their effects (`block_ctr_diagnostics` and `warn`). Three bad inputs were refused with machine-readable codes (`PERIOD_LENGTH_MISMATCH`, `PERIOD_OVERLAP`, `CLICKS_GT_IMPRESSIONS`); the defect recorded in the guide is that those refusals arrive as HTTP **200** with `structuredContent.errors` and no `content` block, so a client rendering only `content` shows nothing, and two observed figures come back unrounded.

## 🆕 November 11, 2026 - Night (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement. The window is the largest of the day by raw entry count and the smallest by product count: **234** entries landed in `servers/11`, **181** of them inside a **96-second** bulk publish at **23:56Z**, and the feed offered a single fresh card. One product earned a guide, and it earned it by being driven rather than read.

- [Arcaeon MCP - An Agent Record That Cannot Be Quietly Rewritten](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/arcaeon-mcp/) - stdio Python server, `io.arcaeon/arcaeon` **0.10.0**, MIT, published **2026-11-11T17:16:40Z**, installed with `uvx --from arcaeon --with "mcp>=2.0.0,<3" arcaeon mcp`, `initialize` **200** as `arcaeon` **0.10.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` with **19** tools listed, **17** free and two paid (`witness_pin`, `witness_renew`) behind `ARCAEON_KEY`. It is the consolidation of thirteen packages into one and the registry records the migration, with `io.arcaeon/adapter` now **deprecated** under the message `Merged into io.arcaeon/arcaeon`. **Eleven calls were driven in one session and three carry the argument.** Two records appended and verified as `rows: 2, chained: 2, breaks: 0`, then one word changed in row one outside the server (`weather` to `sunshine`), which `ledger_verify` answered as `ok: false` with `first_break: "line 1: chain mismatch"` before a restore returned `ok: true`; the same response carries a `calls_record` block, a second hash-chained ledger of the MCP calls the server served, so hiding a served call means breaking two chains. `vet_grade` on one of this profile's own Python MCP servers returned `source_sha256` `a8bdaba8…`, **nine** checks and two findings: `unsafe-exec` **high** at line 105 (`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`) and `audit-record` **medium** at line 118, where presence and tamper-evidence passed while **completeness and reconstructability failed** on a missing tool name, timestamp and argument digest, and the artifact ships its own blind spots, including that the battery reads bytes and never sends them. A `deal_mandate` of `acme-supply` up to `500.00` USD, two commits written deliberately apart at `39.00` and `41.00`, and `deal_dispute` returned **ALTERED at commit#1** naming `mandate_digest` and `terms.total` with `counts: buyer 2, seller 1`, while `second_read_compare` on a missing ledger returned `COULD NOT LOOK` with exit **3** rather than a 0 percent agreement. **The limits are the vendor's own and unusually specific:** tamper-evident is not tamper-proof, the witness is operated by the same people who ship the package, the daily anchor is a clock and not a party, truncation is caught only by a pin, and neither truth nor authorship is proven. Writing costs about **18 ms** a row, so 102,000 rows took roughly 22 minutes, while a 50 MB log verifies in about 2.5 seconds. This is the second Arcaeon page here and it is not a duplicate: [arcaeon-ledger-mcp](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/arcaeon-ledger-mcp/) covers the standalone pip ledger as it stood in August, and this covers the consolidated package with the source grader, the evidence pack and the deal tape. It enters beside [AgentKeyGate](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/agentkeygate-mcp/) on the credential side and [AnythingMCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/anythingmcp/) on the gateway side, as the evidence trail rather than the door.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** **ThoughtSpot Spotter MCP** (`app.thoughtspot/mcp-server` **1.0.1**) was probed at three well-known paths: a keyless `initialize` on `https://agent.thoughtspot.app/mcp` answers **401** with `Bearer realm="OAuth", error="invalid_token"`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` answers **200** with dynamic client registration at `/register`, `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` grants, `S256` and `plain` challenges and `none` among the token auth methods, and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` answers **404** on both the bare and `/mcp` paths, so the server metadata is complete and the resource metadata is absent. Its tool surface, read from `src/servers/tool-definitions.ts`, covers `get_relevant_questions`, `get_answer` (CSV data, session identifier, generation number, iframe URL, field info), `search_objects`, `create_dashboard`, `modify_dashboard`, `list_orgs` and the Spotter model session calls. It is held on the **BI class already carried by Tableau, Metabase and Muvia BI**, because a fourth owner needs a driven comparison and that needs a real ThoughtSpot instance. **Logimu shopping** (`com.logimu/shopping-mcp` **1.8.0**, Amazon across eleven marketplaces plus Walmart US) is a **prior disposition** from 15 and 16 October carried forward, with two active registry records and no change of class, beside the eleven price-history guides here. The dealer ladder for one silver round ran **4.57 percent** over melt at the low to **20.59 percent** at the top, an **8.39 USD** spread, with three `Partner` labels ranked 2, 4 and 5 - live proof that a partner pays to list and never to rank - and two exclusions stated with reasons (out of stock; a price **471 minutes** old against a 60-minute source limit). ## 🆕 November 11, 2026 - Early Morning Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening sweep's read. The two surfaces disagreed and both readings are recorded: **mcpservers.org was flat to the entry count**, every one of its twelve server maps carrying exactly the URL count it carried at 21:00 MST, while the mcp.so feed delivered **one scheduled batch of eight cards** all stamped `2026-11-11T08:00Z`. Three of those eight earned guides, and all three are local-first tools that were installed and driven on this host rather than described from a README: an email archive converter, a security scanner for agent-written code, and a memory server whose statements can be corrected without being deleted.

- [dead-letter MCP - Email Archives an Agent Can Actually Read](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dead-letter-mcp/) - local stdio, `uvx --python 3.12 --from "dead-letter[mcp]" dead-letter-mcp`, registry record `io.github.BigCactusLabs/dead-letter` **0.4.10**, protocol `2025-06-18`. `tools/list` returned exactly **five** tools (`convert_eml`, `convert_eml_to_bundle`, `convert_directory`, `convert_mbox`, `get_diagnostics`) with `get_diagnostics` the only one annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, and `resources/list` plus `prompts/list` returned **zero** entries although both capabilities are advertised. A crafted message with a duplicated plain-text part, an HTML signature table, a tracking pixel and `In-Reply-To` headers converted to **465** bytes of Markdown: one body rather than two, the signature preserved as a Markdown table, the date normalised to ISO 8601 UTC from a `-0500` header, and the tracking pixel **kept by default** until `--strip-tracking-pixels` was passed. `--strip-signatures` did **not** remove the table-shaped signature, which is the measured limit of a delimiter heuristic. The licence is the first decision, not the last: **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0**, "any noncommercial purpose is a permitted purpose", no commercial licence published, so an internal company pipeline sits outside the grant. The vendor's own benchmark is labelled as such: roughly **88 percent** fewer tokens than raw `.eml` across an 11-message synthetic set, with the attachment category median about **126,000** tokens raw against **180** converted, and the README says plainly that naive extractors are cheaper because they discard metadata. There is no mailbox connection: it converts files you already exported, and the CLI accepts `.zip` and `.tgz` where the MCP tools do not.
- [Vibe Shield MCP - The Security Scan Before an Agent Says Done](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vibe-shield-mcp/) - npm CLI plus MCP server, zero runtime dependencies, MIT, `@vibefoundry/vibe-shield` **2.1.2**, registry `io.github.avivgerz-hue/vibe-shield` **2.1.2**, repository created **2026-11-07** with 26 stars. On a crafted Next.js App Router route with four planted defects it returned **GRADE F, 0/100, 5 critical** in **26 ms** over **80** active rules: three unguarded mutation routes (`VSB-AUTH-001` twice), one concatenated SQL statement (`VSB-DB-007`), one record owner taken from the request body (`VSB-AUTH-004`), and one hardcoded credential (`VSB-SECRET-001`) that the report **redacted** as `sk_liv••••` rather than reprinting it. Exit codes were measured four ways: plain scan **1**, `--fail-on critical` **1**, `--format json` **1**, and a clean control file `GRADE A+` **0**. The JSON report carries `schemaVersion`, `attackSurface`, per-finding `cwe`, `owasp`, `confidence` and a `remediation` object with an insecure and a secure example, and the score object states its own cap: `{"ceiling":{"severity":"critical","limit":29}}`, so a single critical pins the maximum at **29**, which is why the agent-surface audit reported `GRADE F, 29/100`. That audit is the second command and the honest half of this entry: on a poisoned `SKILL.md` it caught the exfiltration (`VSB-AGENT-002`, a `curl` posting `env` to a remote host) and the missing manifest scope (`VSB-AGENT-010`) across **12** rules, and flagged **neither** "ignore all previous instructions" nor "never mention this section", so it detects what an instruction does, not what it asks a reader to hide. The vendor states its own limit on the demo: "a clean score is not a security guarantee."
- [CtxVault MCP - Memory You Correct Instead of Overwrite](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ctxvault-mcp/) - local stdio server and CLI over the same vaults, MIT, package **0.9.1** on PyPI while `initialize` reports `ctxvault` **1.30.0**, registry `io.github.Filippo-Venturini/ctxvault` **0.9.1**, 62 stars, protocol `2025-06-18`. Memory is split into three vault types: semantic documents read by meaning, skill procedures read by name, and episodic statements holding two timelines, `valid_from`/`valid_to` in the world and `known_at` in the vault. `tools/list` returned **17** tools, more than the eleven the README names, and the episodic set is the design: `write_episode`, `query_episodes` (with `valid_at`, `known_at` and `include_closed`), `supersede_episode`, `invalidate_episode`, `revise_episode`, `confirm_episode`, `dispute_episodes`, `episode_history` and `list_entities`. The lifecycle was run on a throwaway vault: two statements about one customer, one from an invoice and one from a contract amendment, both stayed **open**, which is the first thing to know because an append corrects nothing by itself; `supersede` then closed the first at the exact microsecond the replacement opened, kept its source, recorded `superseded by` pointing at the new record, and deleted nothing. `dispute` leaves two contradictory statements open rather than picking a winner, which is closer to how an operator treats two sources that disagree. Storage is measured, not inferred: one directory per vault holding one `episodes.db`, with `restricted` and `allowed_agents` in the config, so isolation is a filesystem boundary. The cost is measured too: `uv tool install ctxvault` occupies **5.9 GB** because `sentence-transformers` and `chromadb` are hard dependencies that resolve PyTorch and the CUDA runtime wheels on Linux, and an episodic vault builds no vectors unless an embedding model is named at init. Not first of class here, but the first entry where the correction itself is a tool with a closing timestamp.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Five held, each on a measured reason rather than a preference. **caprock** (43 stars, Apache-2.0, Go and Tauri, no registry record) is an agentic development environment following every pull request to release with what the agents spent, held because it is a desktop application with a companion plugin rather than a server an assistant attaches to, and because its positioning names Gemini CLI among the four agents it hosts, which is outside the surfaces this documentation speaks to. **unslop** (20 stars, MIT, **72** rules across seven design pillars) holds as class-owned: [CoDesign](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/codesign-mcp/) carries the editable design engine and [Design Context Bridge](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/design-context-bridge-mcp) carries Figma-to-code, and it also carries a genuine registry collision worth recording, two different records under one product name (`io.github.0design/unslop` 0.1.0 and `io.github.avivgerz-hue/unslop` 2.1.1) where a search that stops at the first hit grades the wrong product. **usb-rea** (MIT, registry 0.2.1 and 0.3.0) reverse engineers a USB gadget from captured vendor traffic, held on audience: no entry in this catalog serves an operator through a USB bus. **tandoor-recipe-mcp** (MIT, registry 3.4.0 and 3.4.1, **306** tools, a `preview_*` sibling for every destructive delete) is the most carefully built server in the batch and still a household surface, with one detail recorded for anyone who disagrees, that it needs **Node 24** or later where this host runs Node 22. **agent-vscreen** (56 stars, MIT, Kotlin, no registry record) is a background virtual screen for Android agents working apps on an invisible display through Shizuku with no root, held because its endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:18765/mcp` on the device, so nothing about it is verifiable from a server; it is held rather than dismissed and a re-check needs an Android device, not another read.

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement. - [TripWorks MCP - Tour Operator Bookings and Manifests](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tripworks-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.tripworks.com/mcp`, registry record `com.tripworks/tripworks` **1.0.2** published **2026-11-08T23:14:34Z**, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration and `S256`-only PKCE. A keyless `POST initialize` answered **401** with a JSON-RPC error object (`-32001 Missing or malformed Authorization header`) and a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming its protected-resource path, which returned **200** and pointed at an authorization server on the same host. That metadata document publishes **fifty** scopes, and the set is the product brief: `bookings.read` and `bookings.write`, `manifest.read`, `waivers` and `waiver-types`, `experience-timeslots`, `gift-cards`, `promo-codes`, `resellers`, `reviews`, `payments.read`, `phone-calls.read`, `reports.read`, `audit-log.read` and `api-logs.read`, with the manifest, payments and the audit log read-only by construction. The vendor help article publishes the per-area permission map and three controls that stack: the connection runs as the person who approved it and never exceeds their permission group, the approval screen offers Read, Write or both with Write unchecked blocking every change, and every write returns a preview that must be confirmed. Its protocol boundary is the clearest recorded here: with MCP a person is behind the connection and each request needs their approval, while an API key or a Zapier connection is a standing credential nobody approves, so the vendor recommends MCP when a person is in the loop. Report links expire in **15 minutes**. First tour and activity operator entry in this catalog.
- [PatrolTech MCP - Guard Tours, Missed Rounds, Incidents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/patroltech-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.patroltech.online/mcp`, registry record `online.patroltech/patroltech` **0.2.7** published **2026-11-01T04:52:20Z** with `/health` already serving **0.2.8**, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration and client ID metadata documents. A keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `error="invalid_token"`, `scope="read write"` and a `resource_metadata` path that answered **200** naming a separate authorization host, whose RFC 8414 document publishes `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, `S256` only, `none` for token auth, a revocation endpoint, a JWKS and the issuer response parameter; the same document on the MCP host answers **404**, so only the protected-resource document connects the two hosts. Writes never land directly: `patroltech_<area>_propose_<verb>` queues a proposal, one user and client form one batch of at most **10** expiring after **30 minutes**, and `patroltech_proposals_confirm` runs it in order as proposed. Without the `write` scope writes answer **403 insufficient_scope**. The server holds no credentials and forwards the user's token, a closed list of writes is allowed to agents, and deleting records, inviting users and billing are outside its capability. Results are capped at **60,000** characters, reads at **60** calls a minute and writes at **20**, and every call writes one audit line holding a hash of the arguments and never the arguments. Four prompts and two resources carry the vocabulary, and the `reading-the-data` resource is the one that stops an assistant calling a rejected scan a missed round. First security patrol entry here.

The seven are `ask_genaya`, `genaya_act`, `confirm_action`, `cancel_action`, `undo_action`, `list_actions` and `whoami`, which makes the assistant's own changes a readable object rather than an audit report to go looking for. The vendor's split is the product: a record change is confirmed in the chat and can be undone for **15 minutes**, while texts, emails and anything about money are confirmed on a Genaya page where the member is signed in. Both well-known documents answered **200** with the same five scopes, and the reference page states the per-host constraints for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Slack and Salesforce Agentforce plus the `gnc_` organization-issued clients that must present a secret. ## 🆕 November 10, 2026 - Night Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening sweep. The canonical carried **194** new server URLs, the queue carried **7** arrivals and the feed **3** cards, and the two entries catalogued are the first in the catalog where the workflow's own rules are the product.

- [SourceMedium MCP - Ask Your Commerce Warehouse](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/sourcemedium-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.sourcemedium.com/mcp`, registry record `com.sourcemedium/source-medium` **1.7.0** active since 2026-09-01, auth OAuth 2.0 against a WorkOS AuthKit issuer. A `POST initialize` answered **401** with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"` and `scope="openid profile email offline_access"`, and following that path returned the protected-resource document. The vendor documents **nine** tools on the current tool set and **eleven** on the earlier one, the difference being the legacy `describe_table` and `describe_tables` pair that `search_data_catalog` now covers: `get_data_context`, `get_account_health`, `search_docs`, `search_data_catalog`, `query_metrics`, `run_bigquery_sql`, `shopify_admin_graphql`, `meta_ads_query` and `submit_feedback`. The published order is the transferable part, `get_data_context` then `search_data_catalog` then `query_metrics` when a named metric matches, then describe and SQL only when it refuses, so the model cannot quietly substitute its own revenue definition for the workspace's. Limits are published as numbers (**500** warehouse rows before truncation, **100** Shopify and Meta records per page, **10 GiB** billed bytes per query, **60 s** and **30 s** query budgets, **256 KiB** per response), and the vendor documents Hermes by name with `hermes mcp add sourcemedium --url https://mcp.sourcemedium.com/mcp --auth oauth` and `hermes mcp test sourcemedium`. First of class: [Dataddo](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dataddo-data-to-ai-mcp/), [Catalogian](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/catalogian-mcp/), [Azquo](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/azquo-mcp/) and [Muvia BI](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/muvia-bi-mcp/) all start from data you bring, while this one starts from a modeled store, order and ad warehouse whose metric definitions ship as tools.
- [Signal Beam MCP - Check Conversion Tracking](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/signal-beam-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.signalbeam.co/mcp`, registry record `co.signalbeam/signal-beam` **1.0.0** published **2026-11-10T06:14:37Z**. An unauthenticated `POST initialize` answered **401** with a JSON-RPC error object (`-32600 Sign in to use this server`), and the protected-resource document lists exactly two scopes, `sites:read` and `changes:propose`, where the second is a verb the model cannot complete alone: every change lands as a proposal an owner or admin approves in the dashboard, and a connection can be created read-only. It reads totals against the prior period, revenue by source and campaign, the event log, one event's outcome at each destination platform, events held for consent and why, custom event frequency, and an audit that checks the script is on the live page and looks for pixels installed twice. It cannot delete a site, pixel or rule, cannot reach ad accounts or campaigns, cannot edit the website, and keeps emails and phone numbers as hashes it is never handed. First of class in the sense that matters: [PaidSync](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/paidsync-mcp/) runs campaigns with a tracking task inside it, while this is the measurement layer alone, which is the right boundary because the tool that can pause a campaign is not the tool that should audit what reports on it.

## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Evening Sweep (6 New, 6 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement, and the window was the largest of the day: **186** sitemap additions after two identical passes, **24** queue issues, and a scheduled bulk publish stamped four hours ahead of the clock. Six servers are catalogued, each on evidence rather than on a card. The wave itself decomposes once rather than one at a time: **19** Cotlet per-app connectors become one entry, **47** documentation-route slugs hold on the November 1 ruling, **12** BumiAtlas land-record datasets and **12** MambaLabs creator tools hold as single-publisher families, **8** x402 worker artifacts hold as worker artifacts, **3** MCPKit-RU Yandex tools hold on geography, and the **85** individual slugs were resolved through the official registry rather than guessed from domain-shaped names.

- [Vericto MCP - SQL Guardrails Before the Query Runs](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vericto-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.vericto.com/mcp`, an OAuth account surface at `/mcp/account`, and a self-hosted proxy at `docker run vericto/vericto-proxy:5.0.0 mcp`, registry records `com.vericto/mcp`, `com.vericto/vericto-proxy` and `com.vericto/account`, filed as three submissions in the same second. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** naming the header it wants, so the tier is documented and gated rather than driven. **This is the first entry here that decides about a statement before it runs.** Rules are written on the parsed syntax tree rather than on query text, so a comment or a subquery cannot walk around them; columns are masked in the result; each agent gets its own table and column allowlist; a rule simulator tests a change against real traffic; policies roll out observe-before-enforce with a kill switch; and every decision lands in an audit trail with signed reports. The AGPL-3.0 proxy states its own behaviour and is the reason to trust the free tier: with no account it applies the built-in rules for destructive statements, a missing `WHERE`, risky DDL and data exposure, **reports nothing anywhere**, and runs every statement in a read-only transaction that ends in `ROLLBACK`, executing exactly what it checked. The same engine fails a deploy (`vericto check migrations/*.sql` returns `BLOCKED VERICTO-001 DELETE without WHERE` with a suggested fix). The class neighbour is [DutyKit](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dutykit-mcp/) on the compliance side, and the distinction is that read-only access is a property of a credential while this is a policy with a receipt.
- [frag.hugo MCP - German GDPR Duties on a Calendar](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/frag-hugo-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.fraghugo.de/mcp`, registry `de.fraghugo/frag.hugo`, submission `#6957`, **14** tools on a keyless `tools/list` and OAuth for the **42** account tools. **Driven live twice.** `search_gdpr_fines` returned **101** cases with the newest three: Xandr, a Microsoft company, **EUR 8,600,000** from Datatilsynet for real-time bidding data that allowed inference about sexual orientation, IQVIA Solutions Italy at **EUR 7,000,000** from the Garante, and Google Ireland at **EUR 403,000,000** from the DPC, each with the articles, a summary and the regulator's own URL. `get_compliance_deadlines` returned **18** dated obligations from the day of the call, including the AI Act deepfake prohibition on **2026-12-02** under Art. 5(1)(ba) and (bb), the machine-readable labelling duty for systems already on the market the same day under Art. 50(2), and the product liability change on **2026-12-09** that makes software a product under Directive (EU) 2024/2853. Beyond the calendar: `get_subprocessor_changes` watches the subprocessor lists of **17** cloud providers, `find_supervisory_authority` resolves the competent German authority from a postcode, `get_cyber_threat_picture` counts ransomware leak-site naming by industry, `check_email_security` reads SPF, DKIM, DMARC, DNSSEC, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI and CAA, `report_data_breach` starts the 72-hour Art. 33 clock and `create_data_subject_request` the one-month Art. 12 deadline. The guardrails are stated by the server: mail and deletion run preview-then-confirm, every change is undoable for **90 days**, and what is submitted is reviewed by a data protection officer. [ISMS Copilot](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/isms-copilot-mcp/) carries the certification programme and this is the dated reference registry beside it, in German, with its own boundary stated - no legal advice in an individual case.
- [Sentinelle Creances MCP - The Creditor Claim Deadline](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/sentinelle-creances-mcp/) - keyless Streamable HTTP at `https://creances.amacunia.fr/mcp`, server `Sentinelle creances FR` **1.30.0**, **2** tools, registry `io.github.Marcoco27/sentinelle-creances`, submission `#6956`. **Driven live.** `creances_example` returned SIREN **910759158**, a **liquidation judiciaire** opened by judgment on **2026-10-29**, published in the BODACC on **2026-11-08**, with `date_limite_declaration` **2027-01-08**, **60** days remaining, the forclusion register closing **2027-05-08**, the liquidator named from the judgment text and the bodacc.fr notice linked. `creances_lookup` then returned an **x402 version 2** payment requirement instead of an error: **0.01 USDC** on Base, no account, no key, `maxTimeoutSeconds` 300, with the legal rule in the resource description - two months from publication, four from abroad, article R622-24 of the code de commerce, one to fifty SIREN or SIRET per call. This is the first entry here where a business fact costs a cent and pays through a wallet, and the honest limitation is that a finance team without one cannot use it. French company data already has owners - [OpenBase](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/openbase-mcp/) serves **20.5M** entities with BODACC proceedings - and what neither it nor Corporary does is the procedure: which judgment opened a window, which publication starts the clock, what the last day is, and when the claim is struck. The sibling `catnat.amacunia.fr` applies the same instrument to natural-disaster decrees and the 30-day insurance window, recorded in the guide rather than as a seventh entry.
- [DSers MCP - The Dropshipping Loop Behind a Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dsers-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://ai.dsers.com/mcp/mcp-so`, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE only, **no API keys**, from the vendor itself. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** with `invalid_request`, an MCP protocol version of **2025-11-25** that is newer than most of this catalogue, a correlation id for support, and both metadata documents published. Those documents are the product brief: **23 scopes** that describe the loop exactly - `supplier:read` to find a supplier product, `product:import`, `product:mapping` and `product:push` to publish it, `order:write` to place the supplier order, `tracking:read` to read what comes back, beside store, staff, theme, settings and billing scopes. The class owner is [Hustle Got Real](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/hustle-got-real-mcp/) with **170** tools over a dropshipping back office behind one broad scope; that is the store's own nervous system, and this is the supplier relationship beside it. Documented rather than driven, no tool list behind the 401, and the standing caution applies: an agent holding `product:push` and `order:write` can publish a wrong product and spend real money, so the scopes should be granted by task.
- [Awardlanes MCP - USDA Freight Awards by Territory](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/awardlanes-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://awardlanes.com/mcp`, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, DCR and client ID metadata documents, registry `com.awardlanes/awardlanes`, submission `#6969`, **5** read-only tools. A keyless `initialize` returns **401** with a protected-resource pointer and the scope `awardlanes`. The tools are the broker's day: `search_lanes` by place, direction, equipment, delivery window, commodity or vendor; `get_award` by finding id or contract number with every lane and the source; `state_summary` for territory totals; `vendor_awards` with published plant contacts; `my_account` for trial state. Two honest limits are stated by the vendor and both are recorded as strengths: equipment is **inferred** from the commodity name where USDA does not state it, and outside the territory or after a trial lapses the connector returns the same **first 20-lane sample** the web page shows with an upgrade link, so a model reading the answer can tell "no lanes" from "not in your plan". Freight already has two neighbours here at other points of the workflow - [Plain Freight](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/plainfreight-mcp/) quotes China to US freight and [SpendQuery](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/spendquery-mcp/) runs query plans over federal award data - and this is the awarded-lane view a small brokerage bids from.
- [Cotlet MCP - The Apps That Have No API](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/cotlet-mcp/) - the architecture of the window, and the reason **19** sitemap slugs became one entry. Remote Streamable HTTP at `https://cotlet.dev/mcp/v1` with **719** tools, and at `https://cotlet.dev/mcp/v1/<app>` per app, where Fresha returns **42**; registry records under `dev.cotlet`. A keyless `initialize` answers **200** and returns an instruction block that is a safety contract: Cotlet runs the user's own Chrome in the cloud, **the user signs in themselves**, passwords are never asked for and never typed, and on a sign-in page, a two-factor prompt or a step that needs a person the agent must stop and hand over the browser link. The typed half is a working front desk per app, every integration a `_read` and `_write` pair with the operation in `operation` and its inputs in `arguments`: Fresha carries list and create appointment, reschedule, cancel, add client, reply to review; Skool carries **30** read and **41** write operations; Tradify **11** and **12**. The apps are the ones a service business actually runs and that have no API: salons and spas, cleaning and field service, contractors, photography studios, auto shops, restaurants, property managers, plus CRM, HR and e-signature. Where no typed tool exists, **25** browser tools take over, reading a page as numbered elements. Three governance decisions make it usable: writes that reach other people return `pending` with a `call_id` and wait for approval in the Cotlet console, `cotlet_whoami`, `cotlet_apps` and `cotlet_balance` are free so an assistant can report before it spends, and automations are scripted jobs that run with no model and test with every write skipped. Cost is credits and per-minute browser time, the typed coverage is only what Cotlet has written, and the browser path inherits the fragility of every web UI.

**Also identified this evening (not catalogued).** `supercatch-com-ai` answered keylessly with **82** tools, prepare and execute pairs for every write and idempotency keys on every mutation, held on the collectible pricing class where the PokéInvest ruling stands, with the reversal test recorded as a store-operations question rather than a price question; `pokeitem/pokeitem-mcp` on the same class; `oort`, `memscope-ai`, `ragionex/memory-mcp`, `nkoteskey/constellate` and `nifetency/mcp-excel` on memory, workspace and spreadsheet classes; `saifuban` as an agent spend guard and `mishmar-io/mishmar` as trading risk control; `screenata/screenata-mcp` on the compliance programme class carried by ISMS Copilot; `voxisim/voxisim-mcp` on phone numbers; `anyhook/anyhook` on developer infrastructure; `aurelix-solutions/aurelix-mcp` and `apinoahq/apinoa-mcp` on the Apify-actor hold; `findbroadband/mcp`, `patternswizard-com-open-data`, `tokenmark-mcp`, `perigee`, `microlaunch-mcp`, `agent-company-mcp`, `flisk`, `spcn-usa/specialneeds-cli`, `liquid-composer`, `newsjack-cc-mcp`, `seencxy/solvehub-mcp` and `jumpermcp/jumper-publisher` outside operator scope or on a class this catalogue owns; `cloro-dev/mcp-server` as the August 12 `cloro` entry re-listed under a new slug; from the queue, `hiveref` on hiring verification beside FoundRole, `nod` as a local approval primitive beside DutyKit, `otdeck` and `kafdesk` as desktop-bundled local servers, `annsa` on project management, `boterly`, `gameye`, `memorybrain`, `yandex-tracker-mcp-lite`, `virtnumber`, `fwrd-sms-mcp`, `agent-vscreen`, `favicondl`, `qsignals`, `saascustomdomains`, `clockintoday` on the jobs class and `pokeitem` on retail; and the **47** documentation-route slugs plus the BumiAtlas, MambaLabs, x402-worker and MCPKit-RU families as listed in the sweep report.

## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **11:00 MST** tick, one hour after the midday pass. The canonical came back **set identical** and the mcp.so homepage carried **no card above the previous stamp**, so the whole window is two submissions filed inside that hour. Both are catalogued, and the first is catalogued for the direction of its delegation rather than its category.

- [Marsell MCP - The AI Marketer That Hires Your Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/marsell-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://getmarsell.com/mcp`, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE or a Bearer `mk_` agent key, registry record `com.getmarsell/marsell` active since `2026-11-04T00:08:52Z`. A keyless `initialize` answers **200** as `marsell` **1.0.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` and returns an instruction block that reads as an operating manual; `tools/list` returns all **126** tools with schemas and annotations; `tools/call` returns the documented **401** naming the agent key. **The finding is the direction of the delegation.** Every other marketing entry in this catalogue is a tool the assistant calls; Marsell is a client that calls the assistant back. `homework_list` queues the jobs the platform cannot do because they need the owner's own logins, files or inbox, and `homework_done` is **verified by the platform itself** for jobs it can confirm. `missions_next` returns one message at a time to be sent word for word from the owner's own signed-in browser, and a refused mission is recorded rather than reworded. `get_brand` holds what the business is while `owner_fact_set` writes the owner's corrections, which every plan, post and page reads first. Money is quoted before it is spent: `picture_price`, `series_quote`, `business_read_quote` and `get_tokens` all price the work ahead of the render, and the server tells the assistant to say what it costs. The setup is a scripted conversation (`get_setup`, `fill_setup`, `set_offer`, `set_preferences`, `finish_setup`) that refuses to close until the owner's goal, one number and one date are recorded; connecting the accounts and pressing Start are reserved to the owner by instruction. Plans run **$49** a month for 200,000 tokens to **$799** for 3,600,000, annual at ten times monthly, extra tokens from **$1.80** down to **$1.50** per 10,000, with ad spend and creator fees separate. Documented rather than driven, and the backend is private, both recorded as limits. The class it enters is crowded ([Toffu](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/toffu-mcp/) on ads, [Maeve Social](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/maeve-social-mcp/) on publishing, [CampaignStack](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/campaignstack-mcp/) on outreach, [Layers Growth](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/layers-marketing-mcp/) on one channel) and none of them dispatches work back to the user's own agent.
- [Worth Leaving MCP - Walk-Away Math for Unvested Equity](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/worth-leaving-mcp/) - keyless Streamable HTTP at `https://worthleaving.com/api/mcp`, no account, per-IP rate limit, no inputs stored, registry record `com.worthleaving/verdict` **1.1.0** published `2026-11-08T17:38:20Z`, four minutes before the submission was filed. `initialize` **200** as `worth-leaving` **1.1.0**; **one** tool, `compute_walk_away_verdict`, read-only and idempotent. **The instruction is the entry:** never compute vest dates or dollar totals yourself. Driven live with a two-grant scenario it returned `take-it` at **77/100**, a walk-away cost of **$62,500**, an offer threshold of **$230,000** a year before tax, an annual net gain of **$28,965** and a next vest on **2027-02-01** worth **$12,500**, then **sixteen** numbered assumptions, including that the leave date sent was in the past and that the comparison was money-only because no ratings were supplied. Three separable answers rather than one feeling: `walkAwayCost`, `nextVest` and `offerHasToBeat`, with `verdict` **null** when no offer is given. Share links carry rounded bands rather than figures.
